lanes.label: Wrong number reached / customer not on this phone
lanes.claim: These calls are pure contact-data failure, so continued KYC outreach to these numbers only wastes volume and risks customer irritation.
lanes.action: Immediately suppress these numbers for that customer identity and trigger phone-mapping/data-quality review before any further outreach.

lanes.label: No connection made / unreachable customer
lanes.claim: This lane reflects failed reach rather than customer intent, so the main issue is contactability and retry strategy, not KYC process friction.
lanes.action: Reduce repeated same-slot retries and move these cases to smarter redial timing with alternate channels like SMS/app nudges and connectivity-aware retry logic.

lanes.label: Mixed intent lane: explicit refusal, callback requests, and device-access constraints
lanes.claim: This lane mixes customers who should be suppressed with customers who may still convert if contacted at the right time or with basic device-readiness support.
lanes.action: Split handling operationally: suppress explicit refusals, schedule promised callbacks precisely, and give light device/access guidance for the small blocked subgroup.

lanes.label: KYC journey friction: interrupted flow, unclear steps, selfie/camera blocks, mismatch confusion, and weak-network upload failures
lanes.claim: This is the core recoverable conversion lane, showing customers who attempted KYC but got stuck on process clarity, technical steps, or document/data mismatches.
lanes.action: Prioritize recovery messaging and product fixes: resume from the exact failed step, set expectations up front, add selfie/camera and mismatch guidance, and make upload retry resilient on weak networks.

mapCaption: Read left to right from non-signal cleanup, to reachability, to intent handling, to recoverable in-flow KYC friction.

clusters.title: No customer connected
clusters.description: These calls do not contain any customer speech. The line is unanswered or the call fails before a conversation begins, so no KYC blocker can be observed from the customer side.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: No customer language is available because the customer does not speak or the call never connects properly.
clusters.recommendedChange: Reduce repeated voice retries on the same schedule and shift these cases to smarter redial logic with time-of-day testing, alternate channels like SMS or app notifications, and connectivity checks for failed calls.

clusters.title: Stopped mid process, retry later
clusters.description: Customers generally started the KYC flow but dropped off partway through because of upload errors, app hangs, unclear prompts, trust concerns, language difficulty, or uncertainty about the current step. Most are not refusing; they want to resume later, often after office hours.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: They describe a specific point where they got stuck, mention being busy at work now, ask for the link again, and commit to checking in the evening, tomorrow, or weekend.
evidenceQuotes: last mein kuch document upload pe atak gaya tha
Abhi office mein hoon, call pe karna mushkil hai.
mujhe email pe kuch aaya tha aur app pe kuch aur dikh raha tha.
OTP phone pe aaya hi nahi tha
clusters.recommendedChange: Send a resume-focused follow-up with the exact pending step, a trusted app-first path, and short troubleshooting help for common issues like uploads, OTP, signature mismatch, and English comprehension. Time outreach for evenings when these customers say they are free.

clusters.title: Unclear flow and timing
clusters.description: Customers are willing in principle but paused because they did not understand what step was coming, especially video KYC, OTP routing, document choice, or how long the process would take. Many also postponed because they were traveling, in noisy surroundings, or without documents.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: They speak in exploratory, unsure language, asking what the step means, when to do it, how long it takes, or where the OTP will go. They often say they will try later in a better setting.
evidenceQuotes: Video KYC jaisa kuch open hua tha
Time nahi mila honestly.
mujhe samajh nahi aaya ki Aadhaar wala OTP kis number pe jayega
Mujhe video KYC ka option aa raha tha, samajh nahi aaya kab karna hai.
clusters.recommendedChange: Simplify pre-call and in-app guidance around process length, required documents, OTP destination, and when video KYC happens. Add up-front expectation setting like estimated time and a clear checklist before customers start.

clusters.title: Not interested and stop calling
clusters.description: Customers explicitly do not want to do KYC now and frequently object to repeated outreach. Many directly ask for calls to stop, reject explanations, or say they will handle it themselves if ever needed.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: Short, firm refusals. They use direct language about lack of interest, irritation with repeat calls, and not wanting discussion on the phone.
evidenceQuotes: mujhe abhi interest nahi hai
Calls mat kariye baar baar.
Aap log baar baar kyun call karte ho?
Please don't explain anything.
clusters.recommendedChange: Apply strong suppression rules after explicit refusal, reduce repeat-call pressure, and move any remaining outreach to low-frequency passive reminders only where policy allows.

clusters.title: Asked to call back later
clusters.description: Customers are temporarily unavailable rather than resistant. They are in meetings, driving, at a noisy place, or otherwise busy, and they give a specific callback time later the same day or next day.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: Brief scheduling language with concrete callback windows such as after 6 PM, after 7 PM, in 20 minutes, or tomorrow morning.
evidenceQuotes: main meeting mein hoon abhi
6 baje ke baad call kar lena
Main drive kar raha hoon abhi
20 minute baad kar lena
clusters.recommendedChange: Respect and capture the requested callback slot in the dialer workflow instead of reattempting randomly. Keep the later call short and pick up directly from the pending task.

clusters.title: Blocked at selfie or camera
clusters.description: Customers commonly reach the selfie, photo, or face step and get blocked by camera permission confusion, blank camera screens, blurry image rejection, weak front camera issues, or uncertainty about how to start in the app. Many can progress once guided.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: They mention selfie, camera permission, photo blur, blank screen, or not understanding the app entry point. They are usually cooperative and open to retrying later or during the call.
evidenceQuotes: Selfie pe hi atak raha tha, camera permission shayad off tha
Camera permission ka kuch issue aa raha tha.
Camera permission diya tha but kuch blank aa raha tha.
PAN ka photo blur bol raha tha.
clusters.recommendedChange: Add a dedicated pre-selfie help layer: clear permission prompts, camera readiness checks, sample acceptable photo guidance, and a resume experience that restarts from the selfie step instead of the full flow.

clusters.title: Name or address mismatch confusion
clusters.description: Customers drop off when entered identity details do not match documents or when address proof requirements are unclear. Common issues are initials versus full name, middle name differences, old Aadhaar address, current versus permanent address, and uncertainty about acceptable proof.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: They describe mismatch-type errors and ask cautious clarification questions because they want to avoid rejection. They usually intend to continue after understanding which details or documents to use.
evidenceQuotes: mujhe complete karna tha but name mismatch jaisa kuch aa raha tha.
Current address aur Aadhaar address same nahi tha.
Name mismatch aa raha tha PAN pe.
Aadhaar mein purana address hai aur current alag hai.
clusters.recommendedChange: Make mismatch handling explicit in the workflow with examples for initials, middle names, old versus current address, and accepted address proofs. Show field-level tips before submission and explain how to proceed when documents differ.

clusters.title: Wrong contact number reached
clusters.description: The campaign is reaching people who are not the intended customer. Respondents clearly say the named person is not at this number, sometimes noting that the number belongs to them and that they have received such calls repeatedly.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: Direct wrong-number correction, often naming the intended person and denying any connection to them. Some express frustration about repeated mistaken calls.
evidenceQuotes: Nahi, wrong number hai. Yahan Neha nahi hain.
Yahan koi Pooja nahi hai.
mujhe aise calls aate rehte hain
aap baar baar call kar rahe ho.
clusters.recommendedChange: Immediately suppress these numbers from further KYC outreach for that customer identity and trigger data-quality review on phone mapping and source records.

clusters.title: Upload fails on weak network
clusters.description: Customers are willing but run into document upload, selfie, video, or PDF submission failures that appear tied to unstable connectivity or upload processing. They often plan to retry later on Wi-Fi or after getting a fresh link.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: They describe spinners, refresh loops, reconnect messages, image unclear errors, or uploads failing on mobile data. The tone is frustrated but still intent on completing.
evidenceQuotes: Selfie ke baad spinner hi chalta raha.
Mobile data. Network thoda patchy tha.
video step pe network issue aa raha tha. Baar baar reconnect bol raha tha.
It kept spinning, then said something went wrong.
clusters.recommendedChange: Add network-aware guidance and recovery: suggest Wi-Fi before upload-heavy steps, preserve progress after failures, support easier retry from the failed upload, and clarify whether to use camera or gallery.

clusters.title: Device or access issue
clusters.description: These calls reflect practical access constraints: broken camera, camera permission off, laptop-to-phone handoff confusion, OTP going to another phone, or being away from the needed device. A smaller subset also shows low willingness to engage right now.
clusters.customerLanguagePattern: They talk about which device to use, lack of camera access, SIM or OTP being on someone else's phone, or needing another phone to continue. Some responses are curt and mood-based.
evidenceQuotes: mere phone mein camera theek nahi hai.
during the live face check my camera permission was off.
Maine laptop pe khola tha, then bola switch to phone for camera.
OTP dusre phone pe aata hai, SIM mere father ke paas hoti hai.
clusters.recommendedChange: Add a device-readiness check before starting, clearly state that camera steps require a phone, and provide save-and-resume guidance for customers who need access to another device or SIM-linked phone.
